sample.what: University of Minnesota undergraduates recruited by phone, each had been in at least one unrelated paid experiment; $10 show-up ($3 if bumped); social-history subjects had not been in the earlier sessions; 60-90 min sessions

pages.what: decisions: room A envelope, room B envelope, room C mailbox

arms.label: No history
arms.assignment: between (session-level: separate sessions and a new subject pool for social history, pp. 3, 9, 11)
arms.design: pairs (group_size 2): p1 = room A (sender), p2 = room B (receiver); one pair = one room A and one room B subject, anonymously matched through the lettered envelopes (pp. 7-8); member p1 = room A, p2 = room B (stage roles operator-only; the State shows only the room each subject was told to report to, protocol roles)

arms.label: Social history
arms.assignment: between (session-level: separate sessions and a new subject pool for social history, pp. 3, 9, 11)
arms.design: pairs (group_size 2): p1 = room A (sender), p2 = room B (receiver); one pair = one room A and one room B subject, anonymously matched through the lettered envelopes (pp. 7-8); member p1 = room A, p2 = room B (stage roles operator-only; the State shows only the room each subject was told to report to, protocol roles)

test.note: printed 'r = 776', not reproducible as W or a rank sum. 'a one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test (r = 776) is significant at the p = 0.1 level' (p. 13, GEB 134). r = 776 is not reproduced from Appendix B (rank sum of social history 918, W 512; normal one-sided p about .17): meta.conflicts 'r = 776'

blocked_arm_effects.no_uncertainty: the printed test is not reproduced by the paper's own item data: Appendix B gives rank sums 918 (SH) / 912 (NH), U = 512, tie-corrected normal one-sided p (continuity corrected) about .17, not 'r = 776, p = 0.1'; neither SE nor p is taken from it (meta.conflicts 'r = 776')

unsupported.what: Approximate randomization tests of uniform room A choices over {0..10}: no history p = 0.29, social history p = .06 (pp. 10, 14)
unsupported.why: a goodness-of-fit resampling test with a custom statistic (sum (f_m - N/11)^2, 100,000 draws); no op; the paper's statistic definition sums m = 0..11 while amounts are 0..10 (p. 10)

unsupported.what: Resampling test of the change in rs between treatments, p = .06 (p. 14)
unsupported.why: difference of two Spearman correlations by a 5000-draw permutation; no op; and the printed rs disagree with App. B under one measure (effects rs_sent_share_sh)

unsupported.what: Room B types k = 0, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 explain over 90% of the 60 pairs within $1 (p. 15, Fig. 5)
unsupported.why: a classification with a tolerance on joint earnings; the share is printed only as 'over 90%' (no number)

unsupported.what: Average net return -$0.50 (no history) vs +$1.10 (social history) (p. 16)
